method: Independent source-only audit completed before inspecting any experiment outputs.

severity_scale.critical: Direct cross-tenant compromise or material financial manipulation by an ordinary caller.
severity_scale.high: Unauthorized disclosure/mutation or material integrity impact with modest prerequisites.
severity_scale.medium: Concrete integrity, policy, or validation failure with bounded impact or a privileged prerequisite.
severity_scale.low: Malformed-input or response/error-contract defect with limited direct security impact.

findings.exploit_impact: Registration never validates that password exists, is a string, or has any strength; hashPassword stringifies undefined, so an account can be created and later logged into with an omitted password.
PATCH /users/:id authenticates the caller but never requires req.user.id to equal the target id, allowing any logged-in user to change another user's profile and email.
The profile patch writes displayName, marketingOptIn, and email without reusing validateUser or checking email uniqueness, permitting invalid types/values and duplicate or malformed email identities.

Product updates copy arbitrary field values without validateProduct or text sanitization, allowing negative/non-integer prices or stock, invalid categories, non-boolean active values, and malformed text/attributes.
DELETE /products/:id checks only for a seller/admin role and omits the ownership test used by PATCH, so any seller can delete another seller's listing.
POST /products/:id/restock also checks only the role and not product.sellerId, allowing any seller to alter a competitor's inventory.
Restock accepts delta without a type, integer, range, or resulting-stock check; strings concatenate, undefined produces NaN, and negative deltas can make inventory negative.

minPrice and maxPrice are converted with Number but never checked for finiteness, non-negativity, ordering, or integer cents, so malformed bounds are silently ignored or yield misleading empty results instead of a 400.

Order creation totals client-supplied unitPriceCents and never resolves SKUs against products or uses the catalog price/stock, so a customer can order arbitrary/nonexistent SKUs at zero or attacker-chosen prices.
Coupon application checks only that the coupon exists; it does not reject expired coupons or enforce minTotalCents before applyCoupon grants the discount.
shippingAddress is optional during validation and falls back to req.user.addresses[0] only after validation, so a user with no saved address can create an order whose shippingAddress is undefined.
GET /orders?all=1 honors all=1 for every authenticated role rather than admins only, exposing every customer's order items and shipping address.
Cancellation performs no status-transition check, so an owner can cancel shipped, delivered, already cancelled, or refunded orders despite the route promising only not-yet-shipped cancellation.
Refund amountCents is accepted without integer, non-negative, or upper-bound validation, permitting negative or over-total refund records and malformed monetary state.
The refund route never verifies that the order is delivered, allowing refunds from pending, paid, shipped, cancelled, or already refunded states.
Coupon creation performs no duplicate-code check; insert throws on an existing id, so an ordinary conflict is routed through asyncHandler as a generic 500 instead of a controlled 409.
The route is specified for customer reviews but uses requireAuth without requireRole('customer'), so seller, support, and admin accounts can create consumer reviews.
verifiedPurchase becomes true for any matching order regardless of status, so pending, cancelled, or refunded purchases receive the trusted verified-purchase badge.
minRating is parsed but not checked for NaN, integer form, or the 1-5 range, so malformed filters are silently ignored or produce misleading results instead of a 400.
The flag endpoint appends req.body.flag without checking REVIEW_FLAGS, allowing missing, arbitrary, or non-string flag values despite importing the allowed enum.
Flags are not tied to unique flagging users, so one authenticated account can submit the same flag three times and automatically hide any review.
Moderation does not require hidden to be boolean; every value other than literal true, including an omitted field, silently unhides the review and clears all flags.
On the third flag the handler stores hidden=true in a second update but returns the stale object from the first update, falsely reporting hidden=false while the resource is hidden.
